chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amira, from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

From the rights of a believer upon his brother the believer is that he satiates his hunger, and covers his nakedness, and relieves him from his distress, and pays off his debt. So when he dies, he takes his place among his family and children.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a believer upon his brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the comprehensive social contract of brotherhood (ukhuwwah) in Shia tradition, moving beyond basic charity to include debt settlement and posthumous family care. It reflects the Imami emphasis on mutual responsibility, where fulfilling a brother's rights is akin to fulfilling one's own spiritual obligations, ensuring social stability and mercy in both life and death.
